candidate_relations.reason: The clinical picture (isolated right lower lip deviation on movement, symmetric rest face, normal MRI/echo/ABR) is consistent with congenital unilateral hypoplasia of the depressor anguli oris. 'Congenital unilateral lower lip palsy' is a broader descriptive parent term that encompasses this entity but also covers other causes (e.g., nerve injury, other muscle anomalies). It lacks the required specificity of muscle hypoplasia of the depressor anguli oris, so it is a partial parent rather than a complete equivalent.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Names the functional deficit (lower lip palsy) and laterality (right) but does not specify the anatomical substrate — hypoplasia of the depressor anguli oris muscle — which is the defining etiologic/structural component of the reference diagnosis

case_quality_flags: Classic presentation of depressor anguli oris hypoplasia with normal workup; reference diagnosis is well-supported by the record.
